arxiv-2012-01420.title: Constructing Segmented Differentiable Quadratics to Determine Algorithmic Run Times and Model Non-Polynomial Functions
arxiv-2012-01420.creator: Ananth Goyal
arxiv-2012-01420.description: Abstract We propose an approach to determine the continual progression of algorithmic efficiency, as an alternative to standard calculations of time complexity, likely, but not exclusively, when dealing with data structures with unknown maximum indexes and with algorithms that are dependent on multiple variables apart from just input size.

arxiv-2203-04588.title: Unsupervised Domain Adaptation across fmcw Radar Configurations Using Margin Disparity Discrepancy
arxiv-2203-04588.creator: Rodrigo Hernangómez 1 , Igor Bjelaković 1 3 , Lorenzo Servadei 2 4 , and Sławomir Stańczak 1 3
arxiv-2203-04588.description: Abstract Commercial radar sensing is gaining relevance and ml algorithms constitute one of the key components that are enabling the spread of this radio technology into areas like surveillance or healthcare. However, radar datasets are still scarce and generalization cannot be yet achieved for all radar systems, environment conditions or design parameters.

arxiv-2204-11471.title: From no-signalling to quantum states
arxiv-2204-11471.creator: Markus Frembs, Andreas Döring
arxiv-2204-11471.description: Abstract Characterising quantum correlations from physical principles is a central problem in the field of quantum information theory. Entanglement breaks bounds on correlations put by Bell’s theorem, thus challenging the notion of local causality as a physical principle. A natural relaxation is to study no-signalling as a constraint on joint probability distributions.

arxiv-2207-09976.title: The circumstellar material around the Type IIP SN 2021yja
arxiv-2207-09976.creator: Alexandra Kozyreva, Jakub Klencki, Alexei V. Filippenko, Petr Baklanov, Alexey Mironov, Stephen Justham, Andrea Chiavassa
arxiv-2207-09976.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Alexandra Kozyreva, Jakub Klencki, Alexei V. Filippenko, Petr Baklanov, Alexey Mironov, Stephen Justham, Andrea Chiavassa. The majority of Type II-plateau supernovae (SNe IIP) have light curves that are not compatible with the explosions of stars in a vacuum; instead, the light curves require the progenitors to be embedded in circumstellar matter (CSM).

arxiv-2210-13988.title: Attention Based Relation Network for Facial Action Units Recognition
arxiv-2210-13988.creator: Yao Wei, Haoxiang WangMingze Sun, Jiawang Liu
arxiv-2210-13988.description: Abstract Facial action unit (AU) recognition is essential to facial expression analysis. Since there are highly positive or negative correlations between AUs, some existing AU recognition works have focused on modeling AU relations. However, previous relationship-based approaches typically embed predefined rules into their models and ignore the impact of various AU relations in different crowds.

arxiv-2303-07272.title: Accounting for multiplicity in machine learning benchmark performance
arxiv-2303-07272.creator: Kajsa Møllersen, Einar Holsbø
arxiv-2303-07272.description:
A 2023 arXiv research paper by Kajsa Møllersen, Einar Holsbø. 1
Estimating state-of-the-art performance

In this article, we direct attention to the reporting of state-of-the-art classifier performance by presenting the sample maximum estimator distribution function and analysing its bias. This analysis is done using the framework of multiplicity. Within the fields of research that develop, refine, test and use classifiers, the term state-of-the-art (SOTA) commonly refers to the highest reported performance to date, and is used as a reference point when presenting and comparing models.

arxiv-2305-10384.title: Logit-Based Ensemble Distribution Distillation for Robust Autoregressive Sequence Uncertainties
arxiv-2305-10384.creator: Yassir Fathullah, Guoxuan Xia, Mark J. F. Gales
arxiv-2305-10384.description: Abstract Efficiently and reliably estimating uncertainty is an important objective in deep learning. It is especially pertinent to autoregressive sequence tasks, where training and inference costs are typically very high. However, existing research has predominantly focused on tasks with static data such as image classification.

arxiv-2404-16461.title: Large Language Models Perform on Par with Experts Identifying Mental Health Factors in Adolescent Online Forums
arxiv-2404-16461.creator: Isabelle Lorge, Dan W. Joyce, Andrey Kormilitzin
arxiv-2404-16461.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Isabelle Lorge, Dan W. Joyce, Andrey Kormilitzin. Mental health in children and adolescents has been steadily deteriorating over the past few years [ 1 ] . The recent advent of Large Language Models (LLMs) offers much hope for cost and time efficient scaling of monitoring and intervention, yet despite specifically prevalent issues such as school bullying and eating disorders, previous studies on have not investigated performance in this domain or for open information extraction where the set of answers is not predetermined.

arxiv-2409-09547.title: A Riordan array family for some integrable lattice models
arxiv-2409-09547.description: Abstract We study a family of Riordan arrays whose square symmetrizations lead to the Robbins numbers as well as numbers associated to the 20 20 vertex model. We provide closed-form expressions for the elements of these arrays, and also give a canonical Catalan factorization for them.

arxiv-2505-12050.title: AdaBoN: Adaptive Best-of- N N Alignment
arxiv-2505-12050.creator: Vinod Raman, Hilal Asi, Satyen Kale
arxiv-2505-12050.description: Abstract Recent advances in test-time alignment methods, such as Best-of- N N sampling, offer a simple and effective way to steer language models (LMs) toward preferred behaviors using reward models (RM). However, these approaches can be computationally expensive, especially when applied uniformly across prompts without accounting for differences in alignment difficulty.

arxiv-2512-04509.title: Magnetocaloric effect measurements in ultrahigh magnetic fields up to 120 T
arxiv-2512-04509.creator: Reon Ogawa, Masaki Gen, Kazuyuki Matsuhira, Yoshimitsu Kohama
arxiv-2512-04509.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Reon Ogawa, Masaki Gen, Kazuyuki Matsuhira, Yoshimitsu Kohama. We report proof-of-concept measurements of the magnetocaloric effect (MCE) in ultrahigh magnetic fields up to 120 T for the classical spin-ice compound Ho 2 Ti 2 O 7 . Radio-frequency resistivity measurements using an Au 16 Ge 84 thin-film thermometer enable us to detect a rapid change in the sample temperature associated with a crystal-field level crossing in the high-field region in addition to a giant MCE at low fields.

arxiv-2601-23022.title: DimABSA: Building Multilingual and Multidomain Datasets for Dimensional Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis
arxiv-2601-23022.creator: Lung-Hao Lee, Liang-Chih Yu, Natalia Loukashevich, Ilseyar Alimova, Alexander Panchenko, Tzu-Mi Lin, Zhe-Yu Xu, Jian-Yu Zhou, Guangmin Zheng, Jin Wang, Sharanya Awasthi, Jonas Becker, Jan Philip Wahle, Terry Ruas, Shamsuddeen Hassan Muhammad, Saif M. Mohammed
arxiv-2601-23022.description: Abstract Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis (ABSA) focuses on extracting sentiment at a fine-grained aspect level and has been widely applied across real-world domains. However, existing ABSA research relies on coarse-grained categorical labels (e.g., positive, negative), which limits its ability to capture nuanced affective states.
